title: Primary ideals in finite normal power-series algebras: vertical or scalar-annihilated
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a field or a complete discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $r\geq1$, and put $R=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $R\hookrightarrow A$ be injective and finite as a module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], where $A$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $Q$ be a nonzero proper primary ideal of $A$, meaning that $xy\in Q$ and $x\notin Q$ imply $y^n\in Q$ for some $n\geq1$. If $\Lambda$ is a field, there is a nonzero $g\in Q\cap R$. If $\Lambda$ is a discrete valuation ring, fix a uniformizer $\pi$ (a generator of its maximal ideal). Then either there is $g\in Q\cap R$ with nonzero image in $(\Lambda/(\pi))[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$, or $P=\sqrt Q$ is a height-one prime of $A$ containing $\pi$ and $Q=P^{(n)}$ for some $n\geq1$. Here $\sqrt Q=\{x:x^n\in Q\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$, height one means that $P\ne(0)$ and no prime lies strictly between $(0)$ and $P$, and $P^{(n)}=\{a\in A:a/1\in P^n A_P\}$, using localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: V 2.2.3 and V 3.2.3(i),(ii), printed pp.65,67: primary-ideal dichotomy; formulated using contractions instead of dimension.

proof.text: The finite-algebra lemma makes $R\hookrightarrow A$ integral. Since $A$ is a domain, $(0)$ is prime, and $(0)\subsetneq Q$ by hypothesis. Apply the strict-contraction assertion of the integral-incomparability lemma with $\mathfrak q=(0)$ and $\mathfrak q'=Q$ (its second ideal need not be prime). Injectivity gives $(0)\cap R=(0)$, hence $Q\cap R\ne(0)$. Choose $0\ne g\in Q\cap R$. This already proves the field case.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion); strict-contraction form in the cited Mathlib leaf. ILO V 2.2.3(ii), printed p.65.

proof.text: Assume now that $\Lambda$ is a DVR. Coefficientwise reduction $\rho:R\to k[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$, $k=\Lambda/(\pi)$, has kernel $\pi R$: all coefficients of a kernel element have the form $\pi b_E$, and $(b_E)_E$ defines a formal series. The target is a domain by the power-series-domain lemma, because $k$ is a field. Thus $\pi R$ is a prime ideal. Also $\pi\ne0$ in $R$, by its constant coefficient. A DVR is Noetherian since every ideal is principal; hence $R$ is Noetherian by the power-series-Noetherian lemma. Applying the principal-ideal height bound to the prime ideal $\pi R$, which is trivially minimal over itself, gives height at most one; the strict chain $(0)\subsetneq\pi R$ gives height exactly one.

source.place: Tag 0306 (lemma-Noetherian-power-series), Tag 00KV (lemma-minimal-over-1)(1); coefficient reduction from the series definition.

proof.text: The prime $P$ is minimal over $\pi A$. Indeed if $T$ is prime with $\pi A\subseteq T\subseteq P$, then $\pi R\subseteq T\cap R\subseteq P\cap R=\pi R$. The integral-incomparability lemma therefore forces $T=P$. Apply the principal-ideal height bound in the Noetherian ring $A$ to conclude that $P$ has height at most one. It contains the nonzero image of $\pi$ (both inclusions $\Lambda\hookrightarrow R\hookrightarrow A$ are injective), so $(0)\subsetneq P$ and its height is exactly one.

Put $B=A_P$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=PB$. It is a local ring with this maximal ideal by the definition of prime localization, Noetherian by the localization-Noetherian lemma, and a normal domain by the localization-normal-domain lemma ($0
otin A\setminus P$). By the localization dimension lemma, $\dim B$ is the supremum of lengths of prime chains of $A$ ending inside $P$; the chain $(0)\subsetneq P$ has length one, and a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\mathfrak p_2\subseteq P$ would give $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq P$, contradicting height one (Step 4). So $\dim B=1$, and the one-dimensional normal local-domain lemma makes $B$ a discrete valuation ring. We check $Q=A\cap QB$. If $a/1\in QB$, combine a finite ideal expression into one fraction $b/s$ with $b\in Q$ and $s
otin P$. Equality $a/1=b/s$ gives $u(sa-b)=0$ for some $u
otin P$; $A$ is a domain, so $sa=b\in Q$. If $a
otin Q$, primaryness applied to $as\in Q$ would give $s^n\in Q$, contradicting $s
otin P$. Thus $a\in Q$; the reverse inclusion is immediate. In particular $QB$ is proper, since otherwise $1\in Q$. It is nonzero: a nonzero $a\in Q$ remains nonzero in the domain localization, as $a/1=0$ would give $sa=0$ for some $s
otin P$.

proof.text: Every ideal of the DVR $B$ is principal, so write $QB=bB$ with $b\ne0$. Choose a uniformizer $\varpi$ of $B$. The unit-times-uniformizer-power lemma gives $b=u\varpi^n$ with $u$ a unit and $n\ge0$. Properness of $QB$ rules out $n=0$, hence $n\ge1$. Therefore $QB=\varpi^nB=\mathfrak m^n=P^nB$: the ideal generated by all products of $n$ elements of $P$ equals the $n$th power of the ideal generated by their images, by distributing finite sums. Taking inverse images under $A\to B$ and using Step 5 yields $Q=A\cap P^nA_P=P^{(n)}$, exactly the second alternative.
